debate_title: Is current AI progress driven mainly by scaling compute, ...

conflicts.point: Whether semiconductor export controls effectively contain frontier artificial intelligence capabilities or merely reroute development through grey-market channels.

positions.stance: Physical semiconductor export controls provide a verifiable chokepoint that limits frontier training runs and prevents unmanaged capability scaling.
Export controls are porous and easily circumvented via grey-market transshipment, failing to halt algorithmic progress while restricting legitimate research.

conflicts.point: Whether governance should prioritize upstream hardware containment or application-layer civil rights audits and liability.

positions.stance: Upstream compute caps are necessary because unaligned optimization and catastrophic systemic risks outweigh immediate application-layer harms.
Focusing on hardware export controls creates a blind spot that ignores pervasive workplace discrimination and bias happening at the application layer today.

verdicts.conflict: Whether semiconductor export controls effectively contain frontier artificial intelligence capabilities or merely reroute development through grey-market channels.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist position relies on documented supply chain routing data showing that advanced chips routinely bypass geographic restrictions through transshipment hubs. Safetyists offer theoretical physical chokepoints but lack comparable empirical proof that customs enforcement can stop illicit silicon flows at scale.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Customs seizure data demonstrating that border enforcement successfully blocks more than ninety percent of illicit advanced chip shipments would tip the balance.

verdicts.conflict: Whether governance should prioritize upstream hardware containment or application-layer civil rights audits and liability.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position accounts for immediate demographic bias and screening errors occurring in deployed systems today. The safetyist counter-argument focuses narrowly on speculative systemic risks while leaving current application-layer harms unaddressed.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that unaligned artificial intelligence systems cause catastrophic harm at a higher frequency than current application-layer bias would validate upstream hardware priorities.
